dalat.best: Dec–Apr — cool, dry highland days; the wet season eases off May–Oct.
dalat.peak: Vietnamese holidays (Tet, late Jan–Feb) and the July domestic peak.
dalat.quiet: Sept–Nov — green, quiet and cheap between the rains.
dalat.climate: Temperate highland (~1,500m) — spring-like all year, wettest May–Oct.
dalat.getting: 30-min flight from Ho Chi Minh City to Lien Khuong, then 30 min to town.
dalat.terrain: Pine-clad climbs, coffee-farm gravel and quiet highland roads.
dalat.tip: Carry a rain shell in the wet season — afternoons can pour.

hagiang.best: Oct–Apr — dry roads and clear passes; Oct–Nov brings the buckwheat bloom.
hagiang.peak: The Oct–Nov flower season and spring holidays.
hagiang.quiet: Late Feb–Mar — quiet roads before the heat.
hagiang.climate: Northern monsoon — dry, cool winters; wet, slip-prone Jun–Aug.
hagiang.getting: 6–7 hr by road from Hanoi (overnight bus or private transfer).
hagiang.terrain: Big karst passes, switchbacks and remote frontier roads.
hagiang.tip: Avoid Jun–Aug — monsoon rain and landslides hit the loop.

onomichi.best: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — mild, dry and the bridges at their best.
onomichi.peak: Cherry-blossom spring (late Mar–Apr) and the autumn colour.
onomichi.quiet: Early summer (Jun) and winter — cool, calm, fewer riders.
onomichi.climate: Mild Setouchi coast — hot humid summers, gentle winters.
onomichi.getting: Shinkansen to Fukuyama or Shin-Onomichi, then ride from the port.
onomichi.terrain: Flat island-hopping cycleway; only the bridge ramps climb.
onomichi.tip: Bikes cross the bridges toll-free through March 2028 — go now.

chiangmai.best: Nov–Feb — cool, dry mornings and perfect climbing weather.
chiangmai.quiet: The green season (Jun–Oct) — warm, wet afternoons, low prices.
chiangmai.climate: Tropical — cool-dry Nov–Feb, hot Mar–May, wet Jun–Oct.
chiangmai.getting: Direct flights to Chiang Mai (CNX); ride from the old city.
chiangmai.terrain: Temple climbs, the Doi Inthanon monster and rolling loops.
chiangmai.tip: Skip Mar–Apr — crop-burning haze blankets the valley.

pokhara.best: Oct–Nov and Mar–Apr — clear Himalaya, dry trails, mild temps.
pokhara.quiet: Winter (Dec–Feb) — crisp and quiet, snow only up high.
pokhara.climate: Sub-tropical valley below the Himalaya; monsoon Jun–Sep.
pokhara.getting: 25-min flight or 6 hr drive from Kathmandu.
pokhara.terrain: Himalayan gravel, big climbs and lakeside spins.
pokhara.tip: Ride Oct–Nov for the clearest Annapurna views; permits needed up high.

ubud.best: Apr–Oct — Bali’s dry season, warm and green.
ubud.quiet: Shoulder Apr–May and Sept–Oct — dry but calmer.
ubud.climate: Tropical — dry Apr–Oct, wet Nov–Mar, warm year-round.
ubud.getting: 60–90 min from Denpasar (DPS) airport to Ubud.
ubud.terrain: Rice-terrace gravel, jungle trails and the Batur descent.
ubud.tip: Start at dawn — beat the heat, humidity and the scooters.

jeju.best: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — mild, dry and the coast at its best.
jeju.peak: Summer holidays (Jul–Aug) and the autumn colour.
jeju.quiet: Late spring and early-autumn weekdays — quiet bikeway.
jeju.climate: Temperate island — humid summers (typhoons in Aug), windy winters.
jeju.getting: Quick flights from Seoul or Busan to Jeju (CJU).
jeju.terrain: A flat-ish 234km coastal bikeway plus Hallasan climbs.
jeju.tip: Ride clockwise for the prevailing wind, and collect the path stamps.

sunmoonlake.best: Oct–Apr — mild, clear and calm on the water.
sunmoonlake.peak: Autumn weekends and the year-round tour-group flow.
sunmoonlake.quiet: Winter weekdays — misty, peaceful and quiet.
sunmoonlake.climate: Mild central mountains — hot summers, typhoon risk Jul–Sep.
sunmoonlake.getting: ~1 hr from Taichung HSR by bus or transfer.
sunmoonlake.terrain: A smooth 29km lakeside loop with optional mountain climbs.
sunmoonlake.tip: Ride early — the over-water bikeways are magic at sunrise.

medellin.best: Dec–Mar and Jun–Aug — the drier windows in the eternal spring.
medellin.quiet: The shoulder rainy months (Apr–May, Sep–Nov) — green and quiet.
medellin.climate: Spring-like all year (~1,500m); wetter Apr–May and Sep–Nov.
medellin.getting: Fly to Medellín (MDE/EOH); the climbs start from the city.
medellin.terrain: Endless Andean climbs from 1,500m up past 3,000m.
medellin.tip: Acclimatise for a day or two before tackling Alto de Letras.

bright.best: Oct–Apr, with autumn (Mar–May) the local favourite — golden colours and crisp, clear climbs.
bright.peak: Summer school holidays (Dec–Jan) and the Bright Autumn Festival (late Apr–May).
bright.quiet: September and early November — mild, uncrowded and great value.
bright.climate: Alpine — warm-to-hot summers (to ~32°C), crisp autumns, cold snowy winters.
bright.getting: ≈4 hr drive from Melbourne; nearest airport is Albury (~1.5 hr).
bright.terrain: Iconic alpine road climbs (Hotham, Mt Buffalo), the Murray to Mountains rail trail and gravel.
bright.tip: In summer, ride early to beat the heat — autumn mornings are pure magic.

adelaide-hills.best: Sept–Nov and Mar–May — mild days, quiet roads and the harvest buzz.
adelaide-hills.peak: Summer and the autumn vintage and festival season.
adelaide-hills.quiet: Winter — green, cool and very quiet (pack a rain layer).
adelaide-hills.climate: Mediterranean — warm dry summers, cool wet winters.
adelaide-hills.getting: 20–30 min from Adelaide’s CBD and airport.
adelaide-hills.terrain: Punchy Hills climbs (Willunga, Corkscrew), wineries and rail trails.
adelaide-hills.tip: Climb Willunga Hill — the Tour Down Under’s famous finish.

beechworth.best: Oct–Apr; autumn for colour, spring for wildflowers and full creeks.
beechworth.peak: Summer holidays and autumn long weekends and festivals.
beechworth.quiet: September and November — warm days, quiet historic streets.
beechworth.climate: Four-season inland — hot summers, frosty winters.
beechworth.getting: ≈3 hr from Melbourne; Albury airport ~50 min.
beechworth.terrain: Gold-country gravel, granite climbs and the Murray to Mountains rail trail.
beechworth.tip: Loop the Beechworth Gorge, then hit the bakery — it’s the law.

noosa.best: Apr–Oct — warm, dry and free of the summer humidity.
noosa.peak: Summer holidays (Dec–Jan) and the mid-year sunshine escape.
noosa.quiet: Feb–Mar and November — fewer crowds, still plenty warm.
noosa.climate: Subtropical — hot, humid (wet) summers; mild, sunny winters.
noosa.getting: ≈30 min from Sunshine Coast airport; 2 hr from Brisbane.
noosa.terrain: Coastal road spins, hinterland climbs to Maleny and gravel options.
noosa.tip: Beat the heat and traffic with a dawn hinterland loop.

derby.best: Oct–Apr — Tasmania’s warm, long-daylight trail season.
derby.peak: Summer and the big enduro race weekends (book early).
derby.quiet: Shoulder spring and autumn — tacky loam and far fewer bikes on trail.
derby.climate: Cool temperate — mild summers, cold wet winters.
derby.terrain: World-class MTB — 125 km+ of flow, tech and descents at Blue Derby.
derby.tip: Ride mid-week to skip the weekend shuttle queues.

girona.best: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — warm, dry and gloriously quiet roads.
girona.peak: Spring (the pros are in town) and high summer.
girona.quiet: Late autumn and winter — mild and calm, café scene still humming.
girona.climate: Mediterranean — hot summers, mild winters, perfect shoulders.
girona.getting: 35 min from Girona–Costa Brava airport; 40 min by train from Barcelona.
girona.terrain: Endless quiet road climbs, gravel in Les Gavarres, the coast nearby.
girona.tip: Coffee at a pro café, then spin up Els Àngels — the local classic.

mallorca.best: Mar–May and Sep–Oct — the classic cycling-camp seasons.
mallorca.peak: Spring training camps and the Jul–Aug beach-tourism crush.
mallorca.quiet: November — empty roads, still warm, cheap flights.
mallorca.climate: Mediterranean — mild springs, hot summers, gentle winters.
mallorca.getting: Palma airport hub; ~45 min to the Tramuntana climbs.
mallorca.terrain: Sa Calobra, the Serra de Tramuntana and flat plains for fast bunches.
mallorca.tip: Do Sa Calobra at dawn, before the tour buses arrive.
